India wants to build a dam powerful enough to help counter China's control over the Brahmaputra's upstream waters. But in Arunachal Pradesh, the project meant to strengthen India's water security has triggered a revolt of its own.
At the centre of the storm is the proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project. The government sees it as a strategic safeguard against China's massive dam in Tibet. But the indigenous Adi community fears the reservoir could swallow ancestral land, disrupt livelihoods and threaten a way of life tied to the Siang River for generations.
